trials.finding: Every earlier fixed beauty view was rendered through Blender's factory AgX view transform at exposure 0 under the three-light evidence rig. On this atlas that combination turned saturated orange fur salmon pink and clipped 33% of subject pixels; the unlit albedo pass of the same atlas was already saturated and reference-like. Blender's OBJ importer also wired the metallic and roughness maps as sRGB and set Specular IOR Level to 1.0 (twice the default), and Hunyuan's GLB carries the same doubled specular as KHR_materials_specular specularColorFactor 2.0.
trials.renderer_change: scripts/blender/render_turnaround.py gained an optional sixth argument: 'factory' reproduces the historical AgX evidence; 'calibrated' renders the beauty and albedo passes with Standard at exposure -1.5, reads metallic/roughness as Non-Color data, and resets specular to the 0.5 default, while the matcap pass keeps the factory transform so clay evidence stays comparable. The pass order was also fixed: matcap now precedes albedo, because the albedo pass removes the lights and had left every matcap view black whenever albedo was requested. Old and new beauty views are not comparable with each other.

trials.reason: Ayric asked about the white shape on the viewer-left eye. Unlit albedo showed the eye art was clean with only the small painted glint the reference carries, so the shape was a specular reflection: Hunyuan left both eye regions at roughness about 0.11 on an otherwise 0.95 head, and the key area light mirrored off the lumpy eye geometry. Only the two glossy components inside the geometry-derived head-front mask (the eyes, 4,235 texels, 0.10 percent of the atlas) were lifted to a 0.7 floor; a third 462-texel glossy speck was left alone by the size threshold. Floors of 0.35, 0.5 and 0.7 were rendered; 0.5 removed the blob but left a grey wash over the iris, 0.7 matched the matte painted-glint style of the reference.
